explanation: A dry, desolate landscape outside Jerusalem where Jesus was led to fast and be tempted by the devil.
A religious practice in which one abstains from food for a period of time to focus on prayer and spiritual growth.
To offer or lure someone into sin; here it refers to the devil's attempt to lead Jesus away from God's will.
The evil, personified enemy of God who tries to lead people away from truth and righteousness.
Biblical texts or quotations; Jesus uses these to resist the devil's temptations by referring to God's word.
People who serve a master; in this context, it refers to the disciples and all believers who follow Jesus' path.
One of the first places where Jesus taught, often associated with the synagogue or a public meeting place for learning.
A physical ailment; Jesus healed many sick people in Galilee as part of his messianic ministry.
An area in northern Israel where Jesus spent much time and performed his first teachings and miracles.
The livelihood of the disciples; Jesus called fishermen like Simon Peter and Andrew to become "fishers of men".
